scenario.title: Aridaea
intro.text:
ARIDAEA - 14 DEC 1948

East of Aridaea, West Macedonia

The liberation of Greek cities is still at the top of our priorities. Your Division will carry out an surprise attack across the Yugoslav border on Aridaea and free the city! If the resistance is broken here, the further advance on Veroea and Edessa is planned. Let's hope that you succeed and meet an unprepared enemy!

GOAL Capture all VH!
header.act: ACT IV — THE WAR IN THE MOUNTAINS
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-27-0-briliant.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.reaction-27-0-briliant.text: The Vitsi objectives were recovered before government forces could consolidate. The DSE has regained a district and not the strategic balance beyond it.
line.reaction-27-1-victory-tactical.text: Korisos and Dispilio fell after hard fighting. The core survives, but every replacement now comes from a population already divided and exhausted.
line.reaction-27-2-lose.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.reaction-27-2-lose.text: The counterstroke failed to restore Vitsi. The next directive will demand a result at Aridaea as if urgency could replace the formations missing here.
line.callback-0.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.callback-0.text: The Vitsi counterattack put flags back in the towns. It also revived the belief that one more fixed battle can alter the political balance. That belief now has your victory behind it.
line.callback-1.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.callback-1.text: The rebuilt Vitsi routes are carrying food and couriers again. Party reports count the days without a visible victory; the battalions count meals. I know which ledger you chose.
line.callback-2.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.callback-2.text: The detachment which covered the Grammos exits has entered Vitsi under its own officers. Retreat made it surer of itself. That is useful and, in young formations, occasionally dangerous.
line.callback-3.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.callback-3.text: The men and caches from the Grammos exits are scattered through the core now. No unit inherited the honour. Several units inherited enough strength to answer roll call.
line.grammos-front-judgment.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.grammos-front-judgment.text: I warned that a fixed Grammos would become a target number. It did. You held it long enough to save something, and long enough for the pilots to learn every path we used.
line.grammos-corridor-judgment.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.grammos-corridor-judgment.text: The formations came out of Grammos. The villages and the claim to territory did not. You saved the instrument, Commander. I am still waiting to see what political result it can produce.
line.earned-decision.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.earned-decision.text: The Vitsi assault group is outside, fed and overconfident. We can keep that edge for Aridaea, or take away its extra ammunition and make certain the rest of the army reaches the town fit to move.
line.earned-decision.choice.strengthen-a: Give the Vitsi veterans and ammunition to the Aridaea assault group.
Give infantry and artillery 15 experience and fully rearm the core.
line.earned-decision.choice.restore-the-: Distribute the Vitsi replacements and stores through the entire core.
Restore every core formation to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition.
line.earned-a-response.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.earned-a-response.text: Keep the group concentrated. A success needs a point sharp enough to enter the town before doubt does.
line.earned-b-response.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.earned-b-response.text: Level the issue. I want every formation able to leave Aridaea, including the ones which do not appear in the first communiqué.
line.scene-0.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.scene-0.text: The quarrel between Belgrade and Moscow has reached the depots. A road open last winter now depends on which capital the frontier guard thinks we obey.
line.scene-1.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.scene-1.text: The Democratic Army does not set its policy by the mood of a frontier guard.
line.scene-2.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.scene-2.text: No. But the wounded still cross through his gate.
line.scene-3.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.scene-3.text: Aridaea can show that the Democratic Army still takes and governs territory. After the reverses, anything less will be described as survival.
line.scene-4.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.scene-4.text: Survival is not an insult when the alternative is a town surrounded by roads we cannot close. Take the stores, take the prisoners, leave before the National Army makes our success convenient.
line.scene-5.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.scene-5.text: The local committee has prepared offices and a prison list. The withdrawal officer has prepared fuel dumps and departure times. Both are waiting outside, and neither will look at the other.
line.decision.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.decision.text: So decide it now. Is Aridaea a centre we hold, or an operation we finish before the counterstroke?
line.decision.choice.hold-aridaea.text: Take Aridaea and organise it as a permanent DSE centre.
line.decision.choice.hold-aridaea.hint: Give infantry and artillery 20 experience and restore the core to at least nine strength with full ammunition.
line.decision.choice.raid-and-withdraw.t: Seize the stores and prisoners, then withdraw on a prepared schedule.
line.decision.choice.raid-and-withdraw.h: Give reconnaissance 20 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.choice-a-0.text: Then cancel the departure schedule. I disagree, but I will not let half the force fight with one foot on the road. Site the antitank guns before the committee hangs its first notice.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.choice-a-1.text: The town is taken, organised, and defended. Authority enters behind the assault; it does not arrive later to explain why the army left.
line.choice-a-2.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.choice-a-2.text: I will take the prison list. No arrest until a name has an accusation beside it. If we mean to govern, we begin there.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.choice-b-0.text: You are choosing another disappearance. Do not expect a captured storehouse to answer the political defeat of abandoning the town.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.choice-b-1.text: No. It answers the military question of whether these battalions exist next month. Loads, routes, departure hours—issue them before the first unit enters the streets.
line.choice-b-2.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-b-2.text: Good. A soldier can complete an hour. He cannot complete a promise that keeps moving farther into 1949.
epilogue.elas-hold-success.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
epilogue.elas-hold-success.text: The first proclamation came off the Aridaea press while the antitank crews were still digging. For a few weeks the town answered those who said the Democratic Army could only hide. It did not reopen the Yugoslav frontier or replace the battalions already gone. In 1949 the fixed fronts broke. The proclamation travelled into exile folded inside a uniform, proof of a state announced and never secured.
epilogue.elas-raid-success.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
epilogue.elas-raid-success.text: The last Aridaea lorry cleared the road before dawn. We took stores, prisoners, and most of the assault force home. Headquarters called the empty town another failure of nerve. In 1949 the Yugoslav frontier closed and aircraft found the roads manoeuvre could no longer replace. More of the army survived because you left. It survived long enough to lose elsewhere.
epilogue.elas-hold-defeat.speaker: Eleni Markou
epilogue.elas-hold-defeat.text: The committee's prison list never left its envelope. We carried the wounded out past offices prepared for a government that did not arrive. Children had crossed north before the last formations; some learned to write home in another alphabet before their parents knew where exile would take them. The frontier closed in 1949, and the survivors went to camps, prisons, exile, or back to villages where questions were dangerous. During the occupation we built authority from almost nothing. In the civil war, we learned how quickly authority can begin demanding everything.
epilogue.elas-raid-defeat.speaker: Petros Manesis
epilogue.elas-raid-defeat.text: The departure times were still legible when the first units came back without their loads. We saved fragments of the force, not the raid. In 1949 the border closed, aircraft watched the remaining roads, and the villages had little left to give. Some men crossed out, some surrendered, and some simply removed the insignia. No final order told us which of them had completed his duty.
